newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products quiet with Rome industry function.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products quiet with Rome industry function.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products stagnated on Friday in a very quiet market as an industry function in Rome absented many key players from the market.

Gasoline remains well supplied, particularly for low octane barrels. Prices were notionally softer in line with a sagging NYMEX screen. Arbitrage trade was seen to the U.S. out of NWE but more trade was not expected without European prices falling further relative to those in the U.S.
Naphtha was weaker. Skikda barrels remain available while material was also thought on offer from Greece and Morocco.
Gas oil was steady but traders said trade was minimal.
Premiums for Russian material were assessed around the quotes fob hi -$2.00/-$1.00.
Low sulphur meanwhile remained firm as a dearth of material amid discreet demand buoyed prices. Premiums for EN590 were quoted around the quotes fob hi +$3.0/+$5.0 level.
"There's nothing going on half the market's away from its desks," said one trader.
High sulphur was quiet but traders said a cargo was sold ex-Bilbao at cif mean Med plus 25 cents, or about $85.25 cif, or the lower end of the quote.

However, traders said some of the weakness reported in the market recently was due to two traders, including the seller of the Bilbao cargo, that tried to drive prices down to pick up cheap cargoes to sell elsewhere.
There was no market at the moment for high sulphur straight-run with traders saying only one 29,000 tonne cargo was on offer, while the two buyers of cracked material seen were said to be relaxed.
